summary: The note describes Alternate Reality Game (ARG) pilgrimages, a tourism trend in which players travel to real-world locations to solve clues in a fictional storyline. It traces the trend to the late-2023 game "The Odyssey Network" and describes events in New York, Paris and Tokyo, plus participant accounts of self-discovery and human connection. It also covers the industry growing around ARG travel and a forward-looking view into 2024.
one_line: ARG pilgrimages, sparked by "The Odyssey Network", turn real-world travel into game-driven journeys of self-discovery, community and a growing tourism industry.
key_facts: On September 3, 2023, a group of strangers in New York City set off on an ARG treasure hunt rooted in a fictional storyline.
Alternate Reality Games have existed since the early 2000s, blending real-world exploration with storytelling in mixed-media puzzles.
The idea of an ARG as a form of pilgrimage took hold with the late-2023 release of "The Odyssey Network".
Julia Steiner and Marcus Yuen created "The Odyssey Network", which can only be advanced by traveling to physical locations and solving digital and tangible clues.
Emily Thompson, a lawyer from Houston, discovered a passion for historical architecture through the game.
On September 28th, over a hundred players converged at Grand Central Terminal for an ARG event.
On October 15th in Paris, a group followed a storyline inspired by the city's literary history through the haunts of famous writers.
On November 4th in Tokyo, participants solved a cyberpunk mystery moving between neon-lit arcades and Shinto shrines.
Joshua Feldman, a software engineer from Seattle, said in a December 10th interview that players see reflections of themselves in the game's characters and decisions.
Zoe Paterson met her close friends through an ARG and said on January 8th, "I've never felt more connected to people, places, and stories."
Well-known ARG legends include the "Lost Composer" puzzle in Vienna and the "Midnight Riddle of Times Square".
Travel agencies specializing in ARG experiences offer packages combining vacation with gaming.
Tourism boards in Edinburgh, Seoul and Los Angeles have begun partnering with game designers to draw visitors and boost local economies.
Some participants go on to change careers, move to new cities or adopt new philosophies after playing.
